notes.summary: Analogy questions test whether you can find the relationship in one pair and apply it to another; classification (odd one out) tests whether you can spot the item that does not share a common property. RRB NTPC and Group D use word, number and letter versions, and most can be solved in under 30 seconds once you know the common patterns.
keyPoints: Common word relations: product : raw material (Paper : Tree, Glass : Sand), instrument : what it measures (Thermometer : temperature, Anemometer : wind speed, Barometer : atmospheric pressure, Hygrometer : humidity), quantity : SI unit (Mass : kilogram, Electric current : ampere), worker : workplace, animal : young one, creature : home.
Number analogies: test squares, cubes, n² ± 1, n³ ± 1, n² + n = n(n + 1), n³ + n, and multiplying or dividing by a fixed number. Example: 12 : 156 (12 × 13) :: 15 : 240 (15 × 16).
Letter positions: A = 1 ... Z = 26. Anchor with EJOTY = 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 instead of counting from A.
Opposite letters add up to 27: A-Z, B-Y, C-X, D-W, E-V, F-U, G-T, H-S, I-R, J-Q, K-P, L-O, M-N.
Letter clusters: check the gap inside each group (+1, +2, alternating +1/−1) and the shift between corresponding letters of the two pairs (KING → LHOF is +1, −1, +1, −1).
Classification: find a property shared by three items — category (unit of length vs volume), number type (prime, square, cube, multiple of 11) or a letter-gap pattern.
Number-pair classification: apply one rule (for example second = first³ + 1) to every pair; the pair that fails is the answer.
traps: Stopping at the first rule that fits the given pair without checking that exactly one option fits it.
Reversing the direction of the relationship (A : B :: C : ? must keep the same order).
Miscounting letter positions; use the EJOTY anchors.
In odd one out, choosing an item that differs in a trivial way (spelling, number of letters) when a stronger category rule exists.
notes.examTip: Turn the first pair into a short sentence (Paper is made from Tree) and test each option in the same sentence; the one that still makes sense is the answer.

questions.explanation:
Paper is made from wood pulp obtained from trees, so the second word is the raw material of the first.
Glass is made mainly from sand (silica).
Answer: Sand.

questions.text: Find the odd one out: Kilometre, Metre, Litre, Centimetre
questions.explanation:
Kilometre, metre and centimetre are all units of length.
Litre is a unit of volume (capacity).
Answer: Litre.

Each letter of ACE moves one step forward: A→B, C→D, E→F.
Apply the same to GIK: G→H, I→J, K→L.
Answer: HJL.

A thermometer measures temperature (instrument : quantity it measures).
An anemometer measures wind speed. (Humidity is measured by a hygrometer and atmospheric pressure by a barometer.)
Answer: Wind speed.

The kilogram is the SI unit of mass.
The ampere is the SI unit of electric current. (Voltage is measured in volts, resistance in ohms and power in watts.)
Answer: Electric current.

K→L (+1), I→H (−1), N→O (+1), G→F (−1): the letters alternately move +1 and −1.
BOLD: B→C (+1), O→N (−1), L→M (+1), D→C (−1).
Answer: CNMC.

questions.text: Find the odd one out: BDF, HJL, MOQ, RTW
questions.explanation:
Write the positions: BDF = 2, 4, 6; HJL = 8, 10, 12; MOQ = 13, 15, 17 — each has gaps of +2, +2.
RTW = 18, 20, 23 has gaps of +2 and +3.
Answer: RTW.

222 = 216 + 6 = 6³ + 6.
Apply the same rule to 7: 7³ + 7 = 343 + 7 = 350.
Answer: 350.

Test one rule on every pair: second number = (first number)³ + 1.
2³ + 1 = 9, 3³ + 1 = 28 and 4³ + 1 = 65 all fit.
5³ + 1 = 126, not 124.
Answer: (5, 124).
